items.title: 60499_Garvin Bushell oral history interview
items.q: I was Lucky Roberts -- in the '30's I played with Lucky Roberts.

ctx.x: musicians work downtown in New York?

Well, yes, sure we did. We worked the Roseland, I told you, we worked the Club Alabam, we worked what was formerly the Little Club. Negro musicians worked all over New York, all over New York, in the restaurants and the small clubs. They didn't work the Palais Royal -- that was the big one where the whites worked. That was a choice spot, but we worked the Arcadia, the Rose-Land, the Empire, I worked all those ballrooms. The Turf Club. Surely, black musicians worked all of them. Snowden's first band was Kentucky…
When you say on their cars --
